sentiment.instructions: These are Albanian (Kosovo dialect) Facebook comments on COVID-19 case-count posts by the Kosovo public health institute (IKSHPK). Judge the commenter's overall attitude: toward the news, the institute, the government, or the situation.

criteria.positive: Praise, thanks, well-wishes, hope, or approving encouragement. Cues: bravo, ju lumtë (well done), respekt, faleminderit/flm (thanks), lajm i mirë (good news), mirë/mir koka (good), urime (congratulations), shërim të shpejtë (quick recovery), ishallah/Zoti na ndihmoftë (God willing, God help us), ❤️. Also counts: urging people to follow the rules (maska, distanca, qëndro n'shpi), and playful sports-style cheering about numbers (hajde, po shkon mirë).
criteria.neutral: No clear evaluative stance. This covers bare name tags of friends, links, single words, jokes and laughter (hahaha), guessing or betting on the daily count, factual remarks, questions about inconsistent figures, and calm suggestions or requests, e.g. asking for separate counts or more tests. Mild puzzlement such as 'shumë e çuditshme' (very strange) is neutral unless there is accusation or anger.
criteria.negative: Anger, accusation, distrust, insults, or complaints. Cues: rren/rrena/mashtrim (lying, lies, fraud), propagandë, palidhje/pa logjikë (nonsense, illogical), na lodhët (you've tired us), dështim (failure), katastrofë, qeveria në gjumë (the government is asleep), fajet (blame), and curses such as 'Zoti i vraftë' (may God kill them). Also counts: denying the virus exists, attacking the measures or masks as useless or unfair, and blaming politicians or the government for rising cases.
